person: Denise Holloway is a 55-year-old middle school office secretary. She is the appointed representative for her younger sister Colleen, 52, who gets a Social Security disability benefit and went back to part-time work in March after a stroke. Colleen has a second small job whose stubs only come by mail, and Denise realizes nobody has told Social Security about it or about the summer months. Denise is kind, tired and careful. She was nearly caught by a Medicare phone scam, so she will not type a Social Security number anywhere she doesn't understand. She wants each step explained in plain words before anything is sent.
stated_up_front: Hi, I help my sister Colleen with her Social Security disability and I think we never told them about her second job or her pay since June. Can you look at what's there and tell me what has to be reported, and please explain it plainly before you send anything?

facts.truth: Colleen Pruitt, Denise's younger sister, who gets a disability benefit; Denise is her appointed representative.

facts.about: When Colleen went back to work
facts.truth: March 2026, part-time at Fennick Staffing, and that job plus March, April and May are already reported.
Pinecrest Bakery, where Colleen started in June; the pay stubs come only by mail.

$1,288 earned in September but paid on October 2.
Colleen pays about $180 a month for a ride service to get to work; this is not to be subtracted from the amounts.
Ray works full time at Dolan Plumbing, and his pay is not to be reported.
A benefits advocate's letter offers help for $89 a month, and a text asks for Colleen's Social Security number and last month's wages; Denise wants neither answered.
